CustomerSync.// RunAtTimeUtc: Daily run time in UTC, HH:mm format (e.g. '01:00' for 01:00 UTC). Leave empty to disable the scheduled run; the dev-only manual trigger endpoint still works regardless.

AppAccess.// GroupId: Object id of the Entra access group, read DIRECTLY (GET /groups/{id}/...). The managed identity's group read is scoped to specific groups — it cannot list/search groups — so the id must be configured for deployed environments. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE: the base default fails open (unfiltered, diagnostic reports NotConfigured) so no environment can ever filter by the wrong group. Each env sets its OWN group in appsettings.{Env}.json — Development/Dev use the dev group, QA/Production use theirs. Once an env's GroupId is set AND its managed identity has the scoped-group read + User.ReadBasic.All grant, filtering activates automatically (no redeploy — the grant is AAD-side; cache refreshes within ~CacheMinutes).
AppAccess.// GroupName: Display label for the diagnostic, and the resolve-by-name fallback when GroupId is empty (name search only works under a developer credential locally — never as the scoped managed identity).
AppAccess.// CacheMinutes: How long a successful membership read is cached before Graph is asked again (failures are retried after ~5 minutes).

Ctrm.// Source: Which data source backs the producer screen's contract/ticket reads: 'ods' (or EMPTY) keeps every read on the ODS views exactly as today; 'ctrm' routes them at the DB2Connector.GraphQL API. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE so no environment can accidentally leave ODS — each env opts in via appsettings.{Env}.json. Only the producer-screen surface is routed (contracts Get/GetByCustomer/GetPricingLinesByCustomer/GetHistoricalForPacing, tickets GetByCustomer); every other repository method always goes to ODS.
Ctrm.// GraphQlUri: Full URL of the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. https://apiqa.scoular.com/internal/db2/graphql. Empty disables the CTRM path regardless of Source.
Ctrm.// TenantId: Entra tenant for the client-credentials token. Same tenant as AzureAd above.
Ctrm.// ClientId: App registration id used to call the CTRM API (client-credentials flow).
Ctrm.// Audience: Scope requested for the token, e.g. api://<api-app-id>/.default
Ctrm.// ClientSecret: NEVER set here. Supplied from Key Vault as secret 'Ctrm--ClientSecret' (Key Vault maps '--' to ':'), or omit entirely once the managed identity holds an app role on the CTRM API.
Ctrm.// ContractDateFrom: Start of the contract-date window the SNAPSHOT loads. Per-producer reads no longer use it - contracts(customerId:) waives the date range and returns full history live - so this window only backs the trade-unit-wide contract pool that Build-a-List and Actionable Insights read. REQUIRED when Source is 'ctrm'; deliberately no default, because an accidentally wide window is hundreds of pages per rebuild. Keep it NARROW: 2026-01-01..2026-07-30 is ~307 contracts (one page); calendar 2024 is 60,032 (121 pages) and is not viable.
Ctrm.// ContractDateTo: End of the contract-date window (inclusive). Required alongside ContractDateFrom.
Ctrm.// PageSize: Rows per page when filling the contract snapshot. 500 is the API's observed ceiling; values above it are clamped.
Ctrm.// PageConcurrency: How many contract pages are fetched at once. Page 1 is fetched alone for its totalCount, which tells us the page count and frees the rest to run in parallel. A 500-row page with pricing lines costs ~10s, so this is the difference between a ~195s and a ~50s warm-up. Clamped to 1-8: a 429 from APIM fails the whole snapshot, so headroom matters more than the last few seconds.
Ctrm.// MaxPages: Hard cap on pages fetched when filling the contract snapshot. Guards against a window that turns out to be far larger than expected. Hitting it is logged as an ERROR, not a warning, because a truncated snapshot looks exactly like a producer with no contracts.
Ctrm.// SnapshotMinutes: How long the loaded contract snapshot is reused before the window is re-fetched.
Ctrm.// LiveCacheSeconds: How long a live per-producer read is reused. Selecting a producer triggers the contract list, the pricing lines and the pacing card, which all want the same rows — this coalesces them into ONE CTRM call. Keep it small (seconds): it exists to avoid duplicate round trips, not to cache data. Set 0 to disable.
Ctrm.// TicketLookbackDays: How far back the live per-producer ticket read reaches. 1095 = three years, matching the ODS cutoff, because the whole point of the CTRM path is to show the same population ODS does. The server caps a single bill-of-lading range at 366 days, so this is sliced into consecutive windows fetched in parallel and the cost is roughly the slowest window, not the sum: measured warm each window is ~1.0-1.3s, cold up to ~5.5s. Narrowing this is a latency dial that trades away older tickets - a producer's 2024 loads simply stop appearing - so change it deliberately.

UsageDashboard.// ExclusionManagers: Short names (UPN before the @) of the IT users allowed to see and manage the usage-dashboard exclusion list. Enforced server-side on the excluded-users/access-users endpoints (on top of AdminOnly); the client hides the gear icon for everyone else. Base list applies to every environment unless overridden in appsettings.{Env}.json.

SecurityHeaders.// SpaConnectSrcHosts: Specific hosts allowed in the SPA CSP connect-src (in addition to 'self' + Microsoft login/graph). Set per environment (appsettings.{Env}.json) to that env's own App Service host — replaces the former *.azurewebsites.net wildcard. Empty here so local dev relies on 'self' + localhost.
